definitions.definition: Values that are universal, rational, natural and verifiable, all-encompassing and lead to harmony.
The participation of a unit in the larger order of which it is a part.
Education that enables living in harmony within oneself and with others.
A process of dialogue between what you are and what you really want to be.
An acceptance that is invariant with time, place and beliefs and is the same for all humans.
The state of harmony within oneself in thoughts and feelings.
The feeling of having or being able to have more than required physical facilities.
Material things needed for nurturing, protection and right utilization of the body.
Understanding harmony at all levels of one's being.
The sentient, conscious entity that co-exists with the material body.
The material instrument used by the Self (I).
The Self (I) sees, decides and enjoys, using the body as instrument.
The powers of the Self (I); their activities are imaging, analyzing and selecting.
Self-regulation: feeling of responsibility of the Self for nurturing, protecting and rightly utilizing the body.
Health: the body acts according to the needs of I and its parts are in harmony.
The Self needs continuous happiness; the body needs physical facility.
A relation between one Self (I1) and another Self (I2).
The foundation value of relationship: feeling of harmony between two selves.
A salient value in human-human relationship among the nine universal values.
Fulfillment of the nine relationship values leading to happiness of both selves.
The human goal of trust in society.
Existence as units submerged in space, mutually fulfilling one another.
Physical, pranic (bio), animal and human orders.
The inherent harmony and enriching relationship among units of nature.
Understanding co-existence in existence.
Ensuring the feeling and thought of co-existence.
Human society living in co-existence from family to world family.
The societal order in which the comprehensive human goal is realized.
Definite, universal human conduct in consonance with universal human values.
The three aspects of ethical human conduct: mulya, niti and charitra.
Living on the basis of knowing, with acceptance of relationship and participation.
The code of ethical conduct of a profession towards the comprehensive human goal.
Harmony in the individual, prosperity in the family, trust in society and co-existence with nature.
The ability to manifest ethical human conduct in profession and life.
Production and technology that are safe, economical and mutually enriching with nature.
